messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a spike in OOMs and tail-latency regressions on model-x when sequence_len>2048. Profiling points at allocator fragmentation + many small frees from KV cache churn.

jules: ugh. can you paste the profiler traces? is this after the recent kernel-selection edits?

sam: yeah same runtime build as last week. profiler snapshot (shortened):
```
GPU memory: 24GB total
Active allocations: 1.8GB
Cached (held) fragments: 6.9GB
Fragmentation ratio: 0.28
Top alloc sizes: [64B..16MB] (lots of tiny 4-256KB churn from KV cache serializations)
OOM attempt: need 3.2GB but free largest block 1.1GB -> fallback->OOM
```

maria: looks like many tiny allocations cause the caching allocator to create many small segments that later can't be coalesced. Did we change batching heuristics to use more interleaved KV updates?

sam: yes — batching now prioritizes lower latency by flushing partial KV writes earlier which increases small alloc/free ops. Also kernel selection for attention now uses a workspace-per-kernel layout that asks for multiple small scratch buffers.

leo: can we try tuning TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF? Two knobs to test: `max_split_size_mb` to avoid tiny fragment windows, and `garbage_collection_threshold` to trigger earlier cache consolidation. Also we have a custom knob `expandable_segments` on our allocator runtime to allow merging adjacent freed segments.

jules: ACK. propose experiment config:
```
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6"
# runtime flag (redwood): --allocator.expandable_segments=true --allocator.workspace_reuse=on
```
Rationale: smaller max_split_size stops splitting large segments into tiny leftovers, GC at 0.6 will aggressively release cached blocks back into reusable pool before fragmentation grows. Workspace reuse reduces transient allocations per kernel.

sam: spun up a canary with that. infra-bot created job 1801240012.

infra-bot: job 1801240012 started: canary cluster (4x A100), model-x seq_len sweep [1024,1536,2048,3072], workload: 60-min steady QPS 50. Logs forwarded to /var/logs/canary/1801240012.log

maria: also add a KV cache pooling layer: preallocate N reusable buffers per model shard and hand out slices instead of allocating on every write. That should cut tiny alloc churn a lot. Can be opt-in via config `kv_cache.buffer_pool_size=64`.

leo: good call. did sam add the pool?

sam: yes, canary used kv_cache.buffer_pool_size=64. results after 1h:
```
- OOMs: 0 (previously 3 across nodes)
- Avg token latency: -3.8%
- P95 latency: -6.1%
- Memory held cached fragments: 3.1GB (was 6.9GB)
- Fragmentation ratio: 0.12 (was 0.28)
```

jules: wow nice. throughput stable?

sam: throughput +4% at same QPS (less wasted retries/fallbacks).

maria: any regressions on other models? we should run small-model smoke tests (embedding workloads) — sometimes GC thrash hurts small workloads.

sam: ran embedding-smoke: no regressions, slight improvement. but note: when we enabled expandable_segments=true we saw a small CPU-side cost (lock contention) in allocator metadata under extreme multi-threaded inference.

leo: we can mitigate with per-device metadata shards (follow-up). For now, default proposal for canary->staging:
- TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF: max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6
- runtime: expandable_segments=true, workspace_reuse=on
- kv_cache.buffer_pool_size=64 (per model shard)

jules: +1. action items:
- sam: please open an RFC with microbench data + canary logs (assign to eng-runtime).
- maria: prototype per-device metadata sharding to remove lock hot path.
- leo: add automated regression suite runs for small-models under these allocator flags.

sam: will do. attaching minimal repro snippet for future debugging:
```
# reproduce loop
for seq in [1024,1536,2048,3072]:
  run_client --model model-x --seq_len $seq --qps 50 --duration 600 \ 
    --env "TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6" \
    --runtime-flags "--allocator.expandable_segments=true --allocator.workspace_reuse=on" \
    --kv-pool 64
```

infra-bot: job 1801240012 completed: success. artifacts: /artifacts/1801240012/

maria: nice. let's roll to staging with monitoring and a soft rollback window. also add a metric for 'cached_fragment_bytes' per GPU to our console.

jules: agreed. posting RFC link in #eng-runtime once sam files it. :thumbsup:

sam: RFC filed: /rfc/2026/allocator-workspace-reuse (summaries + data). I'll schedule a staging rollout tomorrow.

leo: thanks everyone. keep an eye on kernel-selection changes — if kernels start asking for many separate scratch buffers we may need to switch to a single contiguous workspace for attention kernels to avoid fragmentation.

sam: noted. end of thread.
